hypothesis: A 16-row tile with 32 contiguous X lanes and only two Y threads per block is a new launch shape relative to the observed variants. Prior search samples favored 16x4 over 16x8 and 16x16, but a 32x2 block reduces the CTA to 64 threads while increasing each thread to eight output rows and twelve cooperative tile loads. This tests whether a smaller CTA helps scheduling enough to offset greater per-thread work; no speedup is assumed.
notes: The candidate retains the existing stencil, coefficients, buffers, scratch behavior, and full output coverage. It initializes all 24 shared rows before the barrier and applies the specified period-63 mapping only for q < 0 or q > 63. No local build, oracle check, or timing was run; official correctness on signed varying inputs with independent endpoint values and repeated full-run measurement remain for the controller.
transformations: Change the Y output tile to 16 rows and use a 32x2 block, preserving 32 contiguous X lanes while testing a 64-thread CTA and eight outputs per thread.
Cooperatively load all 24 shared rows, including both halos, and wrap coordinates only when q < 0 or q > 63 by exactly 63.
Compute every output row after the shared-memory barrier using the unchanged stencil expression and write the complete output.
